posts.body_html: An anomalous short stemmed flower on S. purpurea ssp. venosa Montgomery Co, NC! Some might think these might not be venosas based on the pic, but they're all expected to have long stems under normal conditions. These short stems happen most frequently with flowers that bloom out of season or are under some sort of environmental/physical stress. This flower opened up in October 2022!

posts.body_html:
Love it.

Purps really are just stunning things. So often overlooked as people thrill to the taller more showy trumpets. But, man, the longer you are around Sarracenia, the more you appreciate the subtle beauty of purps. At least that's the case for me after so many years. And, if you look at them right, they always look deadly. Real lurkers waiting for prey. Honestly, I could be happy growing nothing but my purps.

posts.body_html: Lots of growers are chasing dark colored purpurea venosas that can get near black. Out of probably close to 1000 different clones that I've grown outdoors, a few get dark purple but nothing like purpurea ssp. purpurea, S. black widow or sarracenia 'Black.' That said, with the right care under greenhouse conditions or LED's, I'd bet that this clone can turn near black. It's certainly darker than the rest when grown under identical conditions outdoors:
